comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citigroup disclose expenses related to the FDIC special assessment imposed to recover losses from the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. However, the financial impact and reporting context differ significantly: Citigroup recorded a much smaller current-year expense of $203 million in 2024, whereas Bank of America carried a substantial remaining accrual liability of $1.7 billion as of year-end 2024, down from $2.1 billion in 2023. Citigroup's 2023 expense was far higher at $1,706 million, suggesting different timing or magnitude of initial provisions compared to Bank of America's progressive accrual adjustments.

sentences.text: In 2023, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) issued a final rule to impose a special assessment to recover certain estimated losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) arising from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.
As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, the Corporation's accrual for its estimated share of the FDIC special assessment was $1.7 billion and $2.1 billion.

Citi recorded $203 million and $1,706 million in Other operating expenses for the years ended 2024 and 2023, respectively, related to the FDIC's final rule implementing a special assessment to recover the uninsured deposit losses from the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the firm purchased a portfolio of approximately $15.0 billion of private equity capital call credit facilities (including $9.0 billion of funded loans) from the FDIC's auction of Signature Bank's loans.
comparisons.comparison: While Bank of America discusses the broader FDIC special assessment liability for deposit insurance losses involving Signature Bank, Goldman Sachs discloses a specific transactional interaction with the FDIC regarding Signature Bank: the acquisition of a portfolio of private equity capital call credit facilities (approx. $15.0 billion) from the FDIC's auction of Signature Bank's loans. Unlike Bank of America's ongoing liability accrual for assessment payments, Goldman Sachs' disclosure reflects an asset acquisition opportunity resulting from the same bank failures that triggered the assessments.

comparisons.peer_topic: FDIC special assessments on Deposit Insurance Fund losses
comparisons.peer_summary: Other expense included an increase of $725 million to the FDIC special assessment in Q1 2024 reflecting revised loss estimates, and a $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment in Q4 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase disclose expenses associated with the FDIC special assessment to recover Deposit Insurance Fund losses. Similar to Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase experienced changes in its accrual during 2024, specifically noting a $725 million increase in Q1 2024 due to revised FDIC loss estimates. However, JPMorgan also highlights a significant one-time charge in the prior period (Q4 2023) of $2.9 billion, whereas Bank of America's disclosure focuses on the year-end accrual balance ($1.7 billion) and the start of quarterly collections in Q2 2024.

sentences.text: In 2023, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) issued a final rule to impose a special assessment to recover certain estimated losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund (DIF) arising from the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank.

The estimated losses will be recovered through quarterly special assessments collected from certain insured depository institutions, including the Corporation, and collection began during the three months ended June 30, 2024.
(c) The first quarter of 2024 included an increase of $725 million to the FDIC special assessment reflecting the FDIC's revised estimate of Deposit Insurance Fund losses.
The fourth quarter of 2023 included the $2.9 billion FDIC special assessment.
